record.english: The meditation on neutrality goes like this. First you put your thoughts in an even state, free of feelings of like and dislike, by thinking about someone who is for you a neutral figure: neither your enemy nor your friend. Then you imagine that two people are sitting before you: one of your best-loved friends, and one of your ugliest enemies. Next you think very carefully about how the friend has, in many of your previous lives, taken birth as your enemy and hurt you. You think too about how the enemy has, in so many of your past lives, taken birth as your friend and helped you. This puts your mind in the even state, free of feelings of like and dislike.

record.english: Right now it's absurd to say that these beings have any kind of pure happiness--they don't even have any of the impure kinds. Every single thing they think is happiness is, in its essence, nothing more than pain. They want wantables but don't want to know about doing the good deeds that bring happiness. They want no unwantables but don't want to know about giving up the bad deeds that bring pain. They act ass backwards: they do what they shouldn't and don't what they should. And so my dear aged mothers, these living beings, are made to suffer.

record.english: My spiritual Friend is here to lead the blind; and in my service of him or her I am obliged to do anything required of me, no matter how exhausting, no matter how distasteful--so long as nothing morally wrong is involved.

record.english: Master Purnavardhana presents the eight chapters of the Treasure House as follows: Eight chapters were written to elucidate in detail what is indicated only briefly by the opening words of the texts: "All phenomena, stained or without stain." the first two of the chapters are devoted to a general treatment of stained and unstained phenomena. A detailed presentation of stained phenomena is left to the next three chapters. The third, for example, relates (1) who it is that is so very afflicted, (2) where they live so very afflicted, and (3) how they are so very afflicted. It does so with respective presentations on (1) the five types of beings in the three realms--the world of living beings; (2) the external world--the "vessel" which holds these beings, and (3) the four modes of birth and twelve links of dependent origination. The fourth and fifth chapters describe what it is that makes beings so very afflicted--stained deeds and the mental afflictions.

record.english: The final three chapters give a detailed treatment of unstained phenomena. Chapter Six covers who it is, what kind of person, that is purified; where it is, the place, that he is purified; and how it is, by what stages of realization, that he is purified. Chapter Seven concerns what it is that makes the person pure: as sutra says, "Affliction is something wisdom must destroy." Chapter Eight concerns meditation--that which provides a base for wisdom to rely on--for as sutra states again, "The mind in meditation gleans pure reality."

record.english: As for the interrelation of these chapters, the first presents the general subject matter addressed by the works on knowledge: stained and unstained phenomena. The first chapter makes but a mere mention of the powers and of the way in which caused phenomena arise; thus the following chapter, the second, is devoted to a more detailed treatment of these two points. The subject of the three realms, given only passing mention in these opening chapters, is therefore explored in the third. Some believe that the three realms thus presented are creations of some god, such as the one they call "Powerful"; the following, fourth chapter therefore disproves this idea and shows that the real source is deeds.

record.english: Consider the following three paths without stain: those of seeing, habituation, and no further learning. They are actual knowledge, because They constitute unstained wisdom and its accessories.

record.english: The ultimate-phenomenon stage of the path of preparation does not, however, rely on preliminary levels other than the one mentioned. The stage beyond no leisure is free of stain, whereas the remaining stages are stained--they are levels wherein one's state of realization derives only from making distinctions between more or less subtle levels of experience. Nor can the ultimate stage of the path of preparation ever rely on the desire level, for the stage is one of controlled meditation, and the desire level is not.

record.english: How many heaps does knowledge have, if you count all of those which are attendant to it? Knowledge can be said to have all five heaps, since unstained wisdom comes along with non-communicating form included within unstained restraint. Feeling is present as pleasure of thought if the wisdom relies on the first two concentration levels. Where it relies on the third, mental pleasure is had. Reliance on other levels, of neutral feeling, means that neutral feeling is present. Discrimination is there as an attendant to consciousness of one's thoughts, as well as the heap of other factors--be they mental functions or the factors not associated with mind--along with consciousness.

record.english: Someone may object that it is improper to speak of consciousness of one's thoughts as being "attendant" to unstained wisdom, since mind itself must be considered more primary than mental functions. Generally the relationship is so, but in the context of an ultimate analysis of phenomena wisdom must be treated as the more primary. If the context had been the subject of belief, for example, we could even have considered faith more principal.

record.english: Let us use the form of a logical statement: Consider the accessories to knowledge just mentioned. They may be given the name "knowledge," because They constitute the means or cause of one's achieving actual knowledge.

record.english: Here are the four attributes: 1) The subject matter of the text concerns stained and unstained types of phenomena. It is indicated in the verse with the words "every existing phenomenon." 2) The purpose is to utilize this subject matter to plant, in students' minds, that wisdom which analyzes phenomena in an ultimate way. It is indicated by the words "ultimate analysis." 3) The ultimate goal is to have these students achieve nirvana, both with and without anything remaining. It is indicated indirectly by the entire phrase running from "There's no way..." up to "...without," and on from "this affliction..." up to the word "Thus." 4) A relation exists in that the purpose must be achieved through the subject matter of the work, and the ultimate goal through this very purpose. One may also state the relation as being between the subject matter of the work (that is, all existing phenomena) and the means by which this subject matter is expressed (i.e., the commentary itself).

record.english: The Treasure House of Chim [Chim Jampey Yang's commentary to the Abhidharmakosha] states: Sutra describes three kinds of karma: virtuous karma, non-virtuous karma, and neutral karma. Virtue is that karma which, in the short term, brings you a karmic ripening which is desirable (that is, a feeling of pleasure), and ultimately protects you from suffering (that is, helps you achieve nirvana). Non-virtue is that karma which brings you a karmic ripening which is undesirable (that is, a feeling of pain). A neutral deed, something neither virtuous nor non-virtuous, is that karma which brings you something which is neither desirable nor undesirable. 49 The Asian Classics Institute Course V: How Karma Works Reading Four: The Correlation of Deeds and Their Results

record.english: The "consistent" consequences are as follows. Even if you do manage to escape the realms of misery and take birth as a human, the following respective results occur to you: 1) Your life is short. 2) You don't have enough to live on. 3) You have problems keeping your partner from others. 4) People don't believe what you say, even when you're telling the truth. 5) You lose friends easily. 6) You hear things as bad sounds. 7) No one listens to you. 8) Your personality is dominated by desire. 9) Your personality is dominated by anger. 10) Your personality is dominated by stupidity.

record.english: The Chapter on the True and the Sutra on the Ten Levels state that there are two such consequences for each of the ones given here; even if you do manage to take birth as a human, 1) Your life is short, and you get sick easily. 2) You don't have enough to live on, and what you do have is all just common property with others. 3) The people who work around you are "inconsistent," which here means unreliable, and you find yourself having a lot of competition for your partner. 4) No one believes what you say, even when you are speaking the truth, and others are always deceiving you. 5) The people around you are always fighting against one another, and have an undesirable character. 6) You hear many unpleasant things, and when others talk to you it always seems to you as if they want to start a fight. 7) No one respects what you say--no one thinks that what you say has any particular value, and you are afflicted with a lack of confidence. 8) Your personality is dominated by desire, and you are never satisfied with what you have. 9) You are always finding yourself without help, or never find the help you need; and you are always hurting others, or always being hurt by others. 10) You become a person who keeps harmful views, or a deceitful person.

record.english: One might wonder about something else: Let's talk about the period while you are in the "uninterrupted" stage of the path of seeing [the actual direct perception of emptiness]. I can accept that at this point the negative thoughts eliminated by this path are no longer present, but we would have to say that the negative things eliminated by the path of habituation are still there, in a dormant way. At this particular point in time, the consciousness of the mind is unstained, unaffected by the mental seed which causes the mistaken state of mind where the appearance and actuality of things are different from one another. As such none of these things could lie dormant here, due to its very quality at the time. There is no consciousness of the senses that could act as the basis for those mental seeds, and it would be improper to say that physical form could ever provide such a basis either. According to you, moreover, there's no foundation consciousness. I would have to think then that there is no basis at all where these dormant things could stay. And yet there is no such problem, for at this point in time it is the simple "me" which is providing the basis for the dormant things eliminated by the path of habituation to stay. You can apply this reasoning as well to all the other cases involving things to be eliminated, and the antidotes which eliminate them. ********* Selection Three: The Middle-Way School on the question of where the seeds of karma stay until they give their resu

record.english: If this were not the case, then consider those holy people who lead their lives following the ten virtues, and who are then born into the higher realms, and then experience the pleasures of these realms. And consider too those miserable people who lead their lives following the ten non-virtues, and who are then born into the lower realms, and then experience the sufferings of these realms. Is the difference between them just that they are having some better or worse kind of misperception, and not whether they are experiencing pleasure or pain? This would have to be the case, if your reasoning were correct.

record.english: Suppose you agree that it is only a matter of better or worse misperceptions. Are you saying then that the pleasures of the higher realms don't even exist, and that the pains of the lower realms don't even exist? You must be, if you agree this way.

record.english: In conclusion now, let us consider again these three kinds of beings, each with their different karma, as they sit down together and look at a glass full of something wet and flowing. It's not necessarily true that they must all have valid perceptions which are identical. If they did, then the three beings looking at the glass of water would have to think of the water as a place to live, in the way that a creature living in water would. The three beings as well would have to see the water in the same way that microscopic organisms living in the water, little beings imperceptible to normal visual consciousness, see it with their own visual consciousness. Then too the visual consciousness of microscopic organisms living in the depths of the ocean would have to be a valid perception towards the entire extent of the sea. And certain kinds of near-gods too would have to see weapons as glasses of water, and on and on; the problems raised would be many.

record.english: Again consider this same situation. Even though it is not necessarily true that the valid perceptions are identical, it is possible for there to be three valid perceptions here which happen to be identical. This is because, as we have already established logically, there can be a case where by the force of karma three different objects, each one confirmed by a valid perception, start to exist. And since this is possible, then it is equally possible that, by the force of karma, three equivalent valid perceptions of a vessel could start to exist as well.

record.english: Generally speaking, each of the three objects mentioned--the pus and the other two--are things of the type that block other objects from entering into the space which they themselves occupy. It is no contradiction though to say that, in this situation where the beings are looking this way, they are not objects such that they block other things from entering into the space they occupy. This is true for the following reason. A central mountain of the world which is square in shape, and a central mountain of the world which is round in shape, and the like, are objects such that they block other things from entering the space they occupy. Nevertheless, it is possible for both these things to occupy the space taken up by a single central mountain of the world. A red-hot ball of steel is something that's hot, but consider what happens when a person touches it after he has used the mantra of steel on his hand. The sensation that he feels is not a sensation of heat; on the contrary, it is a sensation of something not heat. record.english: Just how do we describe these four types of deeds? Non-virtue represents a type of deed which is black and ripens into something black. It is black in that its very nature consists of something afflicted. It also ripens into something black, for it ripens forth into an undesirable result.

record.english: Virtue taken in by the realm of form represents a type of deed which is white and also ripens into something white. This is first of all because of its basic nature: it is unmixed with afflicted types of things, within the mental stream in question. And it ripens forth into a desirable result; with the one mental stream, it is not mixed together with any suffering.

record.wylie: 'dod par gtogs pa'i dge ba ni dkar gnag la rnam par smin pa yang dkar gnag pa'i las yin te, rang gi ngo bo nyon mongs can min pas dkar, rgyud gcig la nyon mongs pa dang 'dres pas gnag, 'bras bu yid du 'ong ba 'byin pas rnam smin dkar, rgyud gcig la sdug bsngal dang 'dres pas rnam smin gnag pa'i phyir
record.english: Virtue taken in by the realm of desire represents a type of deed which is both white and black, and which also ripens into something both white and black. Since its basic nature is free of affliction it is white but--since within a single mental stream it is also mixed with afflicted things--it is black as well. It ripens into something white because it gives forth a pleasant result but--since within the particular mental stream this is also mixed with suffering--we can also say it ripens into something black.

record.english: Here is how these deeds are brought to an end. First let's take the twelve types of mental movement had with the four instants known as "the mastery of phenomena," as well as eight instants of the uninterrupted path [part of the path of seeing, the direct perception of selflessness] which is free of desire. These are the deeds that act to bring black deeds to an end, for they function to eliminate all the mental afflictions that relate to the desire realm.

record.english: Next let's take that type which is the mental movement in the ninth instant of the uninterrupted path. This is a deed which acts to end the white and black, first of all because it eliminates desire-realm virtue by means of eliminating the aspiration, or the desire, for it. Secondly, it eliminates all the mental afflictions of the desire realm--the process here being that one stops the hold which retains them.

It is by this that white deeds are brought to an end, for here one eliminates aspiration, that is desire, for virtue of the formless realm. 65 Other Views on the Black and White

Still other groups assert that those kinds of deeds which the path of seeing eliminates are the black ones, while the other deeds that come from the desire are both white and black. We turn next to our fifth group of deeds, which includes those divided on the basis of the person who possesses them. ********* 72 Three Types of Each Path of Action

record.english: Now some make the claim that views involving unstained phenomena or levels which are not comparable cannot cause a person to lose his most basic virtues. The fact though is that this virtue can be lost through all the forms of this view: through those that focus on levels that are comparable or those which are not; through those that focus on unstained phenomena or on those with stain.

record.english: The meditation on neutrality goes like this. First you put your thoughts in an even state, free of feelings of like and dislike, by thinking about someone who is for you a neutral figure: neither your enemy nor your friend. Then you imagine that two people are sitting before you: one of your best-loved friends, and one of your ugliest enemies. Next you think very carefully about how the friend has, in many of your previous lives, taken birth as your enemy and hurt you. You think too about how the enemy has, in so many of your past lives, taken birth as your friend and helped you. This puts your mind in the even state, free of feelings of like and dislike.

record.english: "You have mentioned," one may begin, "sustenance consisting of contact, and so on. Just what is the nature of each of these types of sustenance?" Contact, mental movement, and consciousness that come with stain are each a kind of sustenance. In their unstained form they can't be called sustenance, for sustenance is defined by its function of perpetuating this suffering life, whereas the stainless act to bring it to a stop. As sutra says, It functions to keep alive those beings who have already come out, and to nourish them; it functions to provide aid to those still in the state of seeking their next life.

record.english: The Master though rebuts this position: This could never be correct--first because of the incongruity between the being to which the name supposedly refers and the nature of the name itself. Moreover, in no sutra or classical commentary at all do we see bodhisattvas who have reached the state conducive to their certain separation from suffering referred to as bodhisattvas residing in the dzambu-tree grove. Therefore the being in question is a bodhisattva who has managed to develop the first concentration level sitting at the base of a dzambu tree, and who has gained his every goal. From the point of view of his having overcome any desire for the objects of the desire realm, the bodhisattva is in no way distinguished from the non-Buddhists mentioned. His vast superiority is nonetheless reflected in the fact that giving to this single person constitutes so much greater merit than giving to the hundred others.

record.english: These afflictions in turn lead you to harmful deeds done in your acts, your words, and your thoughts: deeds like the ten non-virtues, and the five "immediate" deeds, and the five that are close to these, and giving up the highest Dharma, and on and on. Every single day then deeds like these, of tremendous power, capable of leading you to the sufferings of the three lower realms and the like, will tend to increase, further and further. The antidote for all these deeds is the nectar of the Dharma, spoken so true, and the further you turn from it then the more tightly you strangle your chances for the higher realms, and ultimate good. Death will rip away your life, and the wrong deeds you have done will drag you to the lower realms, to a fearful place of mighty and savage suffering, to the fires. And so I ask you, where could you find any thought more disastrous for you than this idea, that what is impermanent could be permanent?

record.english: Master Purnavardhana presents the eight chapters of the Treasure House as follows: Eight chapters were written to elucidate in detail what is indicated only briefly by the opening words of the texts: "All phenomena, stained or without stain." The first two of the chapters are devoted to a general treatment of stained and unstained phenomena. A detailed presentation of stained phenomena is left to the next three chapters. The third, for example, relates (1) who it is that is so very afflicted, (2) where they live so very afflicted, and (3) how they are so very afflicted. It does so with respective presentations on (1) the five types of beings in the three realms-- the world of living beings; (2) the external world--the "vessel" which holds these beings, and (3) the four modes of birth and twelve links of dependent origination. The fourth and fifth chapters describe what it is that makes beings so very afflicted-- stained deeds and the mental afflictions.

record.english: The final three chapters give a detailed treatment of unstained phenomena. Chapter Six covers who it is, what kind of person, that is purified; where it is, the place, that he is purified; and how it is, by what stages of realization, that he is purified. Chapter Seven concerns what it is that makes the person pure: as sutra says, "Affliction is something wisdom must destroy." record.english: As for the interrelation of these chapters, the first presents the general subject matter addressed by the works on knowledge: stained and unstained phenomena. The first chapter makes but a mere mention of the powers and of the way in which caused phenomena arise; thus the following chapter, the second, is devoted to a more detailed treatment of these two points. The subject of the three realms, given only passing mention in these opening chapters, is therefore explored in the third. Some believe that the three realms thus presented are creations of some god, such as the one they call "Powerful"; the following, fourth chapter therefore disproves this idea and shows that the real source is deeds.

record.english: Here are the four attributes: 1) The subject matter of the text concerns stained and unstained types of phenomena. It is indicated in the verse with the words "every existing phenomenon." 2) The purpose is to utilize this subject matter to plant, in students' minds, that wisdom which analyzes phenomena in an ultimate way. record.english: Sutra describes three kinds of karma: virtuous karma, non- virtuous karma, and neutral karma. Virtue is that karma which, in the short term, brings you a karmic ripening which is desirable (that is, a feeling of pleasure), and ultimately protects you from suffering (that is, helps you achieve nirvana). Non-virtue is that karma which brings you a karmic ripening which is undesirable (that is, a feeling of pain). A neutral deed, something neither virtuous nor non-virtuous, is that karma which brings you something which is neither desirable nor undesirable. We return next to the commentary of His Holiness the First Dalai Lama: 16 Deeds according to Result

record.english: The Chapter on the True and the Sutra on the Ten Levels state that there are two such consequences for each of the ones given here; even if you do manage to take birth as a human, 1) Your life is short, and you get sick easily. 2) You don't have enough to live on, and what you do have is all just common property with others. 3) The people who work around you are "inconsistent," which here means unreliable, and you find yourself having a lot of competition for your partner. 4) No one believes what you say, even when you are speaking the truth, and others are always deceiving you. 5) The people around you are always fighting against one another, and have an undesirable character. 6) You hear many unpleasant things, and when others talk to you it always seems to you as if they want to start a fight. 7) No one respects what you say--no one thinks that what you say has any particular value, and you are afflicted with a lack of confidence. 8) Your personality is dominated by desire, and you are never satisfied with what you have. 9) You are always finding yourself without help, or never find the help you need; and you are always hurting others, or always being hurt by others. 10) You become a person who keeps harmful views, or a deceitful person.

record.english: One might wonder about something else: Let's talk about the period while you are in the "uninterrupted" stage of the path of seeing [the actual direct perception of emptiness]. I can accept that at this point the negative thoughts eliminated by this path are no longer present, but we would have to say that the negative things eliminated by the path of habituation are still there, in a dormant way. At this particular point in time, the consciousness of the mind is unstained, unaffected by the mental seed which causes the mistaken state of mind where the appearance and actuality of things are different from one another. As such none of these things could lie dormant here, due to its very quality at the time. There is no consciousness of the senses that could act as the basis for those mental seeds, and it would be improper to say that physical form could ever provide such a basis either. According to you, moreover, there's no foundation consciousness. I would have to think then that there is no basis at all where these dormant things could stay. And yet there is no such problem, for at this point in time it is the simple "me" which is providing the basis for the dormant things eliminated by the path of habituation to stay. You can apply this reasoning as well to all the other cases involving things to be eliminated, and the antidotes which eliminate them. 24 The Middle-Way School on the Question of Where the Seeds of Karma Stay until They Give their Result

The fact though is that this virtue can be lost through all the forms of this view: through those that focus on levels that are comparable or those which are not; through those that focus on unstained phenomena or on those with stain.

record.english: Right now it's absurd to say that these beings have any kind of pure happiness--they don't even have any of the impure kinds. Every single thing they think is happiness is, in its essence, nothing more than pain. They want wantables but don't want to know about doing the good deeds that bring happiness. They want no unwantables but don't want to know about giving up the bad deeds that bring pain. They act ass backwards: they do what they shouldn't and don't what they should. And so my dear aged mothers, these living beings, are made to suffer. "How good it would be if they could all find every happiness, and every cause of happiness. I wish they could. I'll see that they do." "How good it would be if they could all be free of every pain, and every cause of pain. I wish they could. I'll see that they do." Let these two trains of thought run through your mind; meditate on them over and over again. Then you will come to feel the very strongest loving-kindness and compassion. 6 Taking Responsibility Yourself

record.english: "You have mentioned," one may begin, "sustenance consisting of contact, and so on. Just what is the nature of each of these types of sustenance?" Contact, mental movement, and consciousness that come with stain are each a kind of sustenance. In their unstained form they can't be called sustenance, for sustenance is defined by its function of perpetuating this suffering life, whereas the stainless act to bring it to a stop. As sutra says, It functions to keep alive those beings who have already come out, and to nourish them; it functions to provide aid to those still in the state of seeking their next life.

record.english: These afflictions in turn lead you to harmful deeds done in your acts, your words, and your thoughts: deeds like the ten non-virtues, and the five "immediate" deeds, and the five that are close to these, and giving up the highest Dharma, and on and on. Every single day then deeds like these, of tremendous power, capable of leading you to the sufferings of the three lower realms and the like, will tend to increase, further and further. The antidote for all these deeds is the nectar of the Dharma, spoken so true, and the further you turn from it then the more tightly you strangle your chances for the higher realms, and ultimate good. Death will rip away your life, and the wrong deeds you have done will drag you to the lower realms, to a fearful place of mighty and savage suffering, to the fires. And so I ask you, where could you find any thought more disastrous for you than this idea, that what is impermanent could be permanent? 28 The Benefits of Meditating on Death

record.english: The Chapter on the True and the Sutra on the Ten Levels state that there are two such consequences for each of the ones given here; even if you do manage to take birth as a human, 1) Your life is short, and you get sick easily. 2) You don't have enough to live on, and what you do have is all just common property with others. 3) The people who work around you are "inconsistent," which here means unreliable, and you find yourself having a lot of competition for your partner. 4) No one believes what you say, even when you are speaking the truth, and others are always deceiving you. 5) The people around you are always fighting against one another, and have an undesirable character. 6) You hear many unpleasant things, and when others talk to you it always seems to you as if they want to start a fight. 7) No one respects what you say--no one thinks that what you say has any particular value, and you are afflicted with a lack of confidence. 8) Your personality is dominated by desire, and you are never satisfied with what you have. 9) You are always finding yourself without help, or never find the help you need; and you are always hurting others, or always being hurt by others. 10) You become a person who keeps harmful views, or a deceitful person.

record.english: Now there's a big difference here between what we've called “the mind flying off to objects” and this phenomenon of mental agitation. Our mind can fly off to an object during a moment of sheer malice, and we start thinking about some unpleasant object such as a person we don't like. At the same time, the mind can also fly off to a virtuous object—such as an act of giving, or morality—inside of a meditation session as we try to reach quietude. We would call this “the mind flying off,” but we wouldn't call it “agitation.”

record.english: We continue on to the three kinds of close awareness which are unblended.  These are said to be “unblended” in that they are unique. record.english: Now when we are talking here about being in deep meditation which is unstained, there are two ways of looking at it.  According to one, the negative consciousness at this point is engaging only in the unstained.  Another says that—when the deep meditation is being done by a person on the lower way—the negative consciousness still involves the stain of believing that things have some self-nature.  And when the meditation is done by a person on the higher way, then the negative consciousness engages only in the unstained. record.english: A number of masters accept the idea that—in realized beings of the three tracks who are in deep meditation on the unstained—four negative emotions accompanying negative consciousness cannot engage, and remain only in the form of mental seeds.  They say that these are unstained, since they do not have the capacity to make the raw, clear awareness here—the seventh state of mind which represents the substantial flow of negative consciousness in the person's being—something which is stained.

record.acip: [C12] RANG LUGS LA NYAN RANG RNAMS KYI ZAG MED MNYAM GZHAG GI DUS GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED MNGON SUM DU RTOGS PAS NYON MONGS CAN GYI ZAG BCAS SU MI 'JOG KYANG CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN DANG BCAS PA'I DBANG DU BYAS PA'I ZAG BCAS SU 'JOG TSUL SOGS GONG DU BSHAD PA LTAR RO,,
record.wylie: [c12] rang lugs la nyan rang rnams kyi zag med mnyam gzhag gi dus gang zag gi bdag med mngon sum du rtogs pas nyon mongs can gyi zag bcas su mi 'jog kyang chos kyi bdag 'dzin dang bcas pa'i dbang du byas pa'i zag bcas su 'jog tshul sogs gong du bshad pa ltar ro
record.english: According to our own position, listeners and self-made buddhas—when they are in deep meditation upon the unstained—are directly realizing the lack of any self-nature to the person.  As such, their state of mind cannot be established as being stained, in the sense of being involved with the negative emotions.  Nonetheless—as we have explained previously—there is for example a way of positing this state as being stained, insofar as it is possessed of the tendency to believe in the self-nature of things, as opposed to the person.

record.acip: [E34] DE DAG DGE BA'I 'OG TU MI DGE BA DANG KHAMS GONG 'OG ZAG BCAS ZAG MED SOGS SPEL NAS SKYE BAS PHAN TSUN SGO GZHI SGO BYED DU MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR DANG,
record.wylie: [e34] de dag dge ba'i 'og tu mi dge ba dang khams gong 'og zag bcas zag med sogs spel nas skye bas phan tshun sgo gzhi sgo byed du mi rung ba'i phyir dang
record.english: And their unsuitability in this regard is indeed true, because we see certain alternations with the six: first one is virtuous, and then later it becomes non-virtuous; there are variants in the higher realms, and then in the lower realms; and those which are stained, then not stained—and so on.

record.acip: [E47] DE BZHIN DU KUN GZHI MED NA MNYAM GZHAG ZAG MED KYANG MED PAR 'GYUR TE, DE LA GNAS PA'I GANG ZAG MED PAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR TE, YID SHES ZAG MED YIN PAS KHAMS GSUM GANG RUNG GI 'GRO BAR MI 'THAD CING, DE LAS GZHAN GANG ZAG GI MTSAN GZHI KHAS MA BLANGS PA'I PHYIR,
record.wylie: [e47] de bzhin du kun gzhi med na mnyam gzhag zag med kyang med par 'gyur te, de la gnas pa'i gang zag med par 'gyur ba'i phyir te, yid shes zag med yin pas khams gsum gang rung gi 'gro bar mi 'thad cing, de las gzhan gang zag gi mtshan gzhi khas ma blangs pa'i phyir
record.english: In the same manner, there can be no stainless meditation, if there is no foundation consciousness; for if there were such a thing, then there would be no person staying in the meditation. And that would be the case because—since the consciousness of the thoughts would be stainless—then it would be incorrect to say that the person possessing it could exist in any of the three different realms; and we could never accept any representative example of this particular person that was anything else.

record.acip: [E48] DE'I RGYUD LA GANG ZAG GI MTSAN GZHIR GYUR BA'I {%PA'I} YID KYI RNAM SHES SHIN TU PHRA BA YOD CES PAS KYANG SKYON SPONG MI NUS TE, DE 'DRA BA'I RNAM SHES DE ZAG MED SHES PA DANG RIGS MTHUN PA YIN NA SNGAR DRANGS BA'I {%PA'I} MDO DANG 'GAL BAR 'GYUR LA,
record.wylie: [e48] de'i rgyud la gang zag gi mtshan gzhir gyur ba'i {%pa'i} yid kyi rnam shes shin tu phra ba yod ces pas kyang skyon spong mi nus te, de 'dra ba'i rnam shes de zag med shes pa dang rigs mthun pa yin na sngar drangs ba'i {%pa'i} mdo dang 'gal bar 'gyur la
record.english: Now someone may reply, to our last argument, that this individual would possess within their mind the consciousness of their thoughts, which could be considered a representative example of the person. This idea though would not be enough to eliminate the problem we've raised.  For if this type of consciousness were of the same type as the unstained awareness, then that would contradict the sutra we cited earlier.

record.acip: ZAG PA MED PA'I YE SHES ZHES PA'I NGO BO NI, KHA CIG MDZOD NAS BSHAD PA LTAR GYI ZAG PA RGYAS SU MI RUNG BA LA ZAG MED DU 'CHAD PA NI, LUGS 'DI'I ZAG MED DU 'JOG PA'I DON THUN MONG MA YIN PA MA RTOGS PAR SNANG BAS,
record.wylie: zag pa med pa'i ye shes zhes pa'i ngo bo ni, kha cig mdzod nas bshad pa ltar gyi zag pa rgyas su mi rung ba la zag med du 'chad pa ni, lugs 'di'i zag med du 'jog pa'i don thun mong ma yin pa ma rtogs par snang bas
record.english: What then is the essence of immaculate wisdom? Some have glossed “immaculate” here as it is explained in The Treasure House—as referring to an instance where stains can no longer spread. It would appear that these people have failed to grasp the unique way in which something is described as “immaculate” in this particular system.

record.acip: CHAR PHYE BA NA ZHES PA NI CHA CAN ZAG MED KYI YE SHES GCIG NYID KYI CHA SO SO SOR RIM GYIS PHYE BA'I SNGA PHYI'I CHA RNAMS SA SO SOR 'GYUR BA STE,
record.wylie: char phye ba na zhes pa ni cha can zag med kyi ye shes gcig nyid kyi cha so so sor rim gyis phye ba'i snga phyi'i cha rnams sa so sor 'gyur ba ste
record.english: The reference above to “division into certain parts” is meant to convey that there is a single whole: immaculate wisdom. We divide it into sections as it continues on, and thus arrive at progressive parts which we refer to as “bodhisattva levels.”

record.acip: GSUM PA NI, DA NI SNGAR JI SKAD BRJOD PA'I SA RAB DGA' ZHES PA ZAG MED KYI SHES PA'I KHYAD PAR GYIS, SA DE'I YON TAN MDOR BSDUS TE BRJOD PA'I SGO NAS BSTAN PA NI,
record.wylie: gsum pa ni, da ni sngar ji skad brjod pa'i sa rab dga' zhes pa zag med kyi shes pa'i khyad par gyis, sa de'i yon tan mdor bsdus te brjod pa'i sgo nas bstan pa ni
record.english: This bring us to our third and final point from above; that is, we will give a concluding summary of the first level, named Perfect Happiness, by describing its high qualities, singling out the quality of immaculate knowledge.

record.acip: GNYIS PA SA GNYIS PA DRI MA MED PA BSHAD PA LA LNGA, SA 'DIR TSUL KHRIMS YONGS SU DAG PAR BSTAN PA DANG, TSUL KHRIMS KYI BSNGAGS PA BSTAN PA DANG, TSUL KHRIMS KYI MI MTHUN PHYOGS DANG MA 'DRES PA'I DPE BSTAN PA DANG, TSUL KHRIMS KYI PHAR PHYIN GYI DBYE BA BSTAN PA DANG, SA'I YON TAN BRJOD PA'I SGO NAS MJUG BSDU BA'O,,
record.wylie: gnyis pa sa gnyis pa dri ma med pa bshad pa la lnga, sa 'dir tshul khrims yongs su dag par bstan pa dang, tshul khrims kyi bsngags pa bstan pa dang, tshul khrims kyi mi mthun phyogs dang ma 'dres pa'i dpe bstan pa dang, tshul khrims kyi phar phyin gyi dbye ba bstan pa dang, sa'i yon tan brjod pa'i sgo nas mjug bsdu ba'o
record.english: Here is our second division from above, which is an explanation of the second bodhisattva level: Immaculate. This has five parts of its own: a presentation about how, at this level, ones ethical life is completely pure; a presentation of the praises of an ethical life; the presentation of a metaphor to describe how—at this level—ones ethical life is beyond any adulteration by the things that could work against it; a presentation of the divisions of the perfection of an ethical life; and a concluding summary of this level, accomplished by describing its high qualities.

record.acip: DE 'DRA BA'I TSUL KHRIMS 'JIG RTEN PA'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA ZHES BSHAD LA, TSUL KHRIMS DE NYID SNGAR BSHAD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM DU BDEN PAR DMIGS PA'I CHAGS PAS STONG PA STE MI DMIGS PAR RTOGS PA'I ZAG MED KYI SHES RAB KYIS ZIN NA, 'JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS PA'I PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA YIN PAS TSUL KHRIMS LA GNYIS KYI DBYE BA YOD DO,,
record.wylie: de 'dra ba'i tshul khrims 'jig rten pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa zhes bshad la, tshul khrims de nyid sngar bshad pa'i 'khor gsum du bden par dmigs pa'i chags pas stong pa ste mi dmigs par rtogs pa'i zag med kyi shes rab kyis zin na, 'jig rten las 'das pa'i pha rol tu phyin pa yin pas tshul khrims la gnyis kyi dbye ba yod do
record.english: This is the kind of ethical way of life that we call “a perfection of the world.” Suppose though that this same way of life is empty of attachment—in the form of seeing the three spheres we mentioned before as existing in truth; that is, suppose this lifestyle is imbued with immaculate wisdom, where we have realized that these things are non-existent. This then is a perfection which is beyond the world—and so there is a division of ethics into two. Harvest moon

record.acip: ,DE LTAR DGOS PA MED PAR MA ZAD 'JIG RTEN PHA ROL GYI DON DANG YANG NI 'GAL BAR 'GYUR TE, KHONG KHRO LA SKABS BYIN PAS SHI BA'I 'OG TU RNAM SMIN YID DU MI 'ONG BA 'PHEN PA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: de ltar dgos pa med par ma zad 'jig rten pha rol gyi don dang yang ni 'gal bar 'gyur te, khong khro la skabs byin pas shi ba'i 'og tu rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba 'phen pa'i phyir ro
record.english: Not only is the anger thus pointless, but it also contradicts your goals for the world beyond; that is, if you allow yourself feelings of anger, then it will project ahead of you—after your death—an upleasant karmic ripening. Wishes for revenge & to avoid pain are contradictory

record.acip: RANG GI LUS LA GNOD PA'I SDUG BSNGAL CHEN PO DGRA DAG GIS BSGRUBS PA DE NI, SNGON BYAS PA YI SROG GCOD KYI MI DGE BA'I LAS KYI 'BRAS BU, NGAN SONG GSUM DU RNAM SMIN DRAG PO MYONG ZHING, RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU LHAG MAR LUS PA CAN RNAMS KYI, RGYU MTHUN GYI 'BRAS BU YID DU MI 'ONG BA MA LUS PA LDOG PA'I RGYU GANG YIN PA,
record.wylie: rang gi lus la gnod pa'i sdug bsngal chen po dgra dag gis bsgrubs pa de ni, sngon byas pa yi srog gcod kyi mi dge ba'i las kyi 'bras bu, ngan song gsum du rnam smin drag po myong zhing, rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu lhag mar lus pa can rnams kyi, rgyu mthun gyi 'bras bu yid du mi 'ong ba ma lus pa ldog pa'i rgyu gang yin pa
record.english: And so now think about the great pain that people who hate you might be inflicting upon your body. This is the consequence of a negative deed that you've done in the past: the taking of life, and something which you would normally have to experience as a violent karmic ripening in one of the lower realms. It also serves to expiate all the rest of the remaining homogenous results—all the rest of the unpleasant homogenous results.

record.acip: DANG PO NI, MI BZOD PA NI RNAM SMIN YID DU MI 'ONG BA YANGS PA 'PHEN PA'I RGYU YIN PA 'BA' ZHIG TU MA ZAD KYI, YUN RING DU BSAGS PA'I BSOD NAMS KYI TSOGS ZAD PA'I RGYU YANG YIN NO, ZHES STON PA NI,
record.wylie: dang po ni, mi bzod pa ni rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba yangs pa 'phen pa'i rgyu yin pa 'ba' zhig tu ma zad kyi, yun ring du bsags pa'i bsod nams kyi tshogs zad pa'i rgyu yang yin no, zhes ston pa ni
record.english: Here is the first. The author next demonstrates how failing to maintain our patience not only acts as a cause which projects extensive, unpleasant karmic results; but at the same time serves as a cause which wears away the accumulation of good karma that has taken us a very long period of time to put together.

record.acip: DE YI PHYIR DE LTAR NA 'BRAS BU YID DU MI 'ONG BA 'PHEN PA DANG, DGE BA LA GNOD PA BYED PA'I SDIG PA NI, MI BZOD PA KHONG KHRO LAS GZHAN PA'I MCHOG TU GYUR PA YOD PA MA YIN NO,,
record.wylie: de yi phyir de ltar na 'bras bu yid du mi 'ong ba 'phen pa dang, dge ba la gnod pa byed pa'i sdig pa ni, mi bzod pa khong khro las gzhan pa'i mchog tu gyur pa yod pa ma yin no
record.english: And thus—meaning “therefore”—there exists no negative deed which is more effective than anger, losing ones patience, for projecting unpleasant karmic consequences into the future, and for damaging ones good karma.

record.acip: BDEN 'DZIN NYON MONGS SU 'JOG PA'I LUGS 'DI LA, NYON MONGS ZAG MED KYI LAM GYIS SPONG BA NA, BDEN 'DZIN RE'I SA BON SPONG DGOS PAS SA BON DE LAS GZHAN PA'I GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS SHES SGRIB TU BZHAG PA'I PHYOGS RE YANG GTAN ZAD MI NUS PAS, NYON MONGS THAMS CAD MA ZAD BAR DU SHES SGRIB MI SPONG BA'I PHYIR, SHES SGRIB NI DAG PA SA GSUM GYI SKABS SU SPONG NGO,,
record.wylie: bden 'dzin nyon mongs su 'jog pa'i lugs 'di la, nyon mongs zag med kyi lam gyis spong ba na, bden 'dzin re'i sa bon spong dgos pas sa bon de las gzhan pa'i gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags shes sgrib tu bzhag pa'i phyogs re yang gtan zad mi nus pas, nyon mongs thams cad ma zad bar du shes sgrib mi spong ba'i phyir, shes sgrib ni dag pa sa gsum gyi skabs su spong ngo
record.english: Here in this system, where holding that things are real is classified as a negative emotion, each seed of holding things this way must be eliminated where negativities are eliminated by the path of the immaculate. But not all the different propensities for seeing things in a mistaken way—with a discrepancy—which are other than these seeds, and which we classify as obstacles to omniscience, can at that point be eliminated permanently. As such, we cannot rid ourselves of the obstacles to omniscience until we finish off all the negative emotions; and therefore it is during the three pure levels that we rid ourselves of these omniscience obstacles.

record.acip: RANG LUGS LA 'GOG PA MNGON SUM DU SHES PA MNYAM GZHAG ZAG MED KYI YE SHES KYIS, ,DE KHO NA NYID KYI DON RTOGS PA'I STENG NAS BSGRUBS PAS, 'GOG BDEN KUN RDZOB KYI BDEN PA YIN NA RNAM GZHAG DE DAG GTAN MI RUNG ZHING,
record.wylie: rang lugs la 'gog pa mngon sum du shes pa mnyam gzhag zag med kyi ye shes kyis, ,de kho na nyid kyi don rtogs pa'i steng nas bsgrubs pas, 'gog bden kun rdzob kyi bden pa yin na rnam gzhag de dag gtan mi rung zhing
record.english: According to our own school, immaculate wisdom engaged in deep meditation, a direct perception of the end of suffering, sees both the object of suchness and—on top of that—this end. As such, saying that the truth of the end of suffering is part of deceptive reality would—according to this presentation—be completely mistaken.

record.acip: MI SHES PA'I GNYID KYIS YID RAB TU BSKYOD PA'I MU STEGS CAN YID LA PHYIN CI LOG GI GRUB MTHA' NGAN PA DANG, GTAN TSIGS LTAR SNANG GI GNOD PA YOD PA 'DI DAG NI, DE KHO NA NYID LA 'JUG PAR 'DOD PAS SKYE BO MA BYANG BA GNAG RDZI DANG BUD MED LA SOGS PA YAN CHAD LA GRAGS PA'I SKYE BA DANG, 'JIG PA LA SOGS PA PHYIN CI MA LOG PA MA BZUNG BAR, 'JIG RTEN PA RNAMS LAS PHUL DU BYUNG BAR 'GRO BAR 'DOD PAS,
record.wylie: mi shes pa'i gnyid kyis yid rab tu bskyod pa'i mu stegs can yid la phyin ci log gi grub mtha' ngan pa dang, gtan tshigs ltar snang gi gnod pa yod pa 'di dag ni, de kho na nyid la 'jug par 'dod pas skye bo ma byang ba gnag rdzi dang bud med la sogs pa yan chad la grags pa'i skye ba dang, 'jig pa la sogs pa phyin ci ma log pa ma bzung bar, 'jig rten pa rnams las phul du byung bar 'gro bar 'dod pas
record.english: Consider now those of lower views, whose minds are inspired by the sleep of misunderstanding—those with minds adversely affected by mistaken, undesirable schools of thought, or false forms of logic. They wish to rise above the everyday world: they hope to engage in the way things really are. But they want to do so without recognizing things like starting & stopping—in the way these are understood among those who have not applied themselves formally to philosophy, beginning for example from cowherds or women—as being unmistaken.

record.acip: DE'I TSE YID KYI SHES PA NI GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL BA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS MA BSLAD PA'I ZAG MED YIN PAS, DE'I NGO BOR BAG LA NYAL DE GNAS PA MI RIGS LA, DBANG SHES KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MED CING GZUGS KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MI RIGS LA
record.wylie: de'i tshe yid kyi shes pa ni gnyis snang 'khrul ba'i bag chags kyis ma bslad pa'i zag med yin pas, de'i ngo bor bag la nyal de gnas pa mi rigs la, dbang shes kyang de'i rten du med cing gzugs kyang de'i rten du mi rigs la
record.english: At this point though, the awareness of our thought is unstained, in the sense that it is not infected by the deep seeds for the error of the discrepancy. As such, it would be incorrect to say that the seeds were remaining in a dormant state as part & parcel with this awareness. Neither could there be any sense consciousness which were acting as their basis; and it would be illogical to say that physical form itself were providing the base.

record.acip: LUGS 'DI'I GANG ZAG GI 'JOG TSUL THUN MONG MA YIN PA SHES NA NAM MKHA' DANG RNAM SHES MTHA' YAS DANG CI YANG MED PA GSUM DU SKYES PA'I 'PHAGS PA'I RGYUD LA, 'JIG RTEN LAS 'DAS PA ZAG MED KYI SEMS MNGON DU GYUR PA NA, 'JIG RTEN PA'I SEMS GZHAN MED PAS DE RNAMS KYI 'GRO BA LDOG PAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES PA DANG,
record.wylie: lugs 'di'i gang zag gi 'jog tshul thun mong ma yin pa shes na nam mkha' dang rnam shes mtha' yas dang ci yang med pa gsum du skyes pa'i 'phags pa'i rgyud la, 'jig rten las 'das pa zag med kyi sems mngon du gyur pa na, 'jig rten pa'i sems gzhan med pas de rnams kyi 'gro ba ldog par 'gyur ro, zhes pa dang
record.english: If we can come to an understanding of the unique manner in which this particular system posits the person, then it would appear that our position could no longer be challenged by arguments such as the following. The first here would be where someone asks us to consider the mind stream of a realized being who has taken birth into one of the three levels of Limitless Space; Limitless Awareness; or Nothing At All. When a state of mind which transcends the normal world—an unstained state of mind—manifests itself, then since there can be no other, worldly states of mind, their functioning is said to be suspended.

record.acip: SRID RTZER SKYES PA'I 'PHAGS PA LA CI YANG MED PA'I SAR GTOGS PA'I ZAG MED KYI SEMS MNGON DU GYUR PA NA, SRID RTZE DANG CI YANG MED PA GNYIS KA'I SAS BSDUS PA'I 'GRO BA LDOG PAR 'GYUR TE, ZAG MED KYI SEMS DE'I GNAS NI 'GRO BA DE GNYIS DANG, MYANG NGAN LAS 'DAS PA'I 'GRO BAR MI RUNG BA'I PHYIR RO, ZHES GSUNGS PA'I
record.wylie: srid rtser skyes pa'i 'phags pa la ci yang med pa'i sar gtogs pa'i zag med kyi sems mngon du gyur pa na, srid rtse dang ci yang med pa gnyis ka'i sas bsdus pa'i 'gro ba ldog par 'gyur te, zag med kyi sems de'i gnas ni 'gro ba de gnyis dang, myang ngan las 'das pa'i 'gro bar mi rung ba'i phyir ro, zhes gsungs pa'i
record.english: Or else we can consider the case where a realized being has taken birth into the level known as Peak of Existence, but they have manifested an unstained state of mind taken in by the level of Nothing At All. This then blocks any possibility of them passing to a state subsumed by either the Peak of Existence or by Nothing At All, since it would be inappropriate to describe the location of an unstained state of mind as either one of these two types of existence, or as a state of existence within the state of nirvana.

record.acip: RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG MI GNOD PAR MNGON TE, ZAG BCAS DANG ZAG MED KYI SEMS GANG YANG 'GRO BA DE DAG GI MTSAN GZHIR MA BZHAG KYANG 'GRO BA BZHAG PAS CHOG PA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: rigs pa rnams kyis kyang mi gnod par mngon te, zag bcas dang zag med kyi sems gang yang 'gro ba de dag gi mtshan gzhir ma bzhag kyang 'gro ba bzhag pas chog pa'i phyir ro
record.english: The reason that these arguments would no longer be a challenge is that—even though there is no state of mind either stained or unstained which we could point to as a typical example for any of these states of existence—we can nonetheless posit such states.

record.acip: RAB RIB CAN GYI MIG GIS SKRA SHAD SOGS MTHONG BA DANG, BONG BU'I RVA LA SOGS PA MI MTHONG BA'I NGES PA DE'I PHYIR RNAM SMIN YID DU 'ONG BA NI MI DGE BA LAS MI 'BYUNG LA, RNAM SMIN YID DU MI 'ONG BA NI DGE BA LAS MA YIN PA'I PHYIR, RNAM SMIN MI DGE BA STE YID DU MI 'ONG BA NI, NAG PO'I LAS LAS YIN LA, RNAM SMIN DGE BA STE YID DU 'ONG BA NI DGE BA LAS 'BYUNG BA YIN PAR MTHONG ZHING,
record.wylie: rab rib can gyi mig gis skra shad sogs mthong ba dang, bong bu'i rva la sogs pa mi mthong ba'i nges pa de'i phyir rnam smin yid du 'ong ba ni mi dge ba las mi 'byung la, rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba ni dge ba las ma yin pa'i phyir, rnam smin mi dge ba ste yid du mi 'ong ba ni, nag po'i las las yin la, rnam smin dge ba ste yid du 'ong ba ni dge ba las 'byung ba yin par mthong zhing
record.english: Eyes affected by cataracts see things like strands of hair; but it is definite that they do not see things like horns on top of the head of a rabbit. As such, it is not the case that a pleasant ripening of karma can come from a non-virtuous deed; and neither can an unpleasant ripening come from a virtuous deed. We can see then that a non-virtuous ripening—an unpleasant one—is something that comes from a black karma; while a virtuous ripening—a pleasant one—is something that comes from a good deed.

record.acip: ,BDAG NI GZUGS LDAN MI 'DOD GANG PHYIR BDAG, ,YOD MIN DE PHYIR LDAN DON SBYOR BA MED, ,GZHAN NA GNAG LDAN GZHAN MIN GZUGS LDAN NA, ,BDAG NI GZUGS LAS DE NYID GZHAN NYID MED,
record.wylie: bdag ni gzugs ldan mi 'dod gang phyir bdag, ,yod min de phyir ldan don sbyor ba med, ,gzhan na gnag ldan gzhan min gzugs ldan na, ,bdag ni gzugs las de nyid gzhan nyid med
record.english: We do not accept That the self is something That could possess form; Why we say so Is that there is no Possibility of the self; Therefore the point of The connection possessed By them is not something That could exist. Suppose it were To something being other: “He is possessed of a blackie.” Suppose he was possessed Of a physical form where There was no separate thing. The relationship of the self To the form is neither the same; Nor are they essentially different.

record.acip: 'DI LTAR LDAN PA'I RKYEN YANG LHA SBYIN GNAG STE BA LANG DANG LDAN NO ZHES PA LTA BU NI, GZHAN NA STE NGO BO THA DAD PA LA SBYOR LA,
record.wylie: 'di ltar ldan pa'i rkyen yang lha sbyin gnag ste ba lang dang ldan no zhes pa lta bu ni, gzhan na ste ngo bo tha dad pa la sbyor la
record.english: The fact that we could have this kind of factor here is something similar to the way in which we say that “John is possessed of a blackie” (referring to a kind of dark-colored cow). Which is to say, suppose we made the reference here to something being other, or essentially separate.

record.acip: SANGS RGYAS KYI CHOS NI, MA 'DRES PA BCU DANG BRGYAD DU GANG 'DOD PA DE DAG GZHAN GYIS MI 'PHROGS PA'I RANG GI MTSAN NYID CAN TE, RGYU MTSAN GANG GI PHYIR NA STON PA LA MA 'DRES PA'I MI MTHUN PHYOGS 'KHRUL PA SOGS MI MNGA' BAS DE RNAMS KYIS GLAGS MED PA NYID KYIS MI 'PHROGS PA STE, THUB PAR MI NUS PA DE'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: sangs rgyas kyi chos ni, ma 'dres pa bcu dang brgyad du gang 'dod pa de dag gzhan gyis mi 'phrogs pa'i rang gi mtshan nyid can te, rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na ston pa la ma 'dres pa'i mi mthun phyogs 'khrul pa sogs mi mnga' bas de rnams kyis glags med pa nyid kyis mi 'phrogs pa ste, thub par mi nus pa de'i phyir ro
record.english: The Dharma of the Buddhas, which we assert has those 18 qualities of being unmixed, has an own quality that it cannot be stolen off by others. The reason why this is true is that the Teacher has no nature of being mixed in with things like error, or ideas that would contradict their positions. As such, their teachings cannot be “stolen off,” or defeated—for that simple reason that they cannot be defeated.

record.acip: MA 'DRES PA'I NGES TSIG NI CHOS DE RNAMS SANGS RGYAS KHO NA'I RTEN LA YOD KYI, RTEN GZHAN LA MED PAS RTEN MA 'DRES PA'O,,
record.wylie: ma 'dres pa'i nges tshig ni chos de rnams sangs rgyas kho na'i rten la yod kyi, rten gzhan la med pas rten ma 'dres pa'o

record.english: When you want to do a meditation to master these points, here is a brief description of how to proceed, through the practice of giving and taking: Remember the text that says to "let these two ride on the wind"; For this you take the breath that passes out of both your nostrils And give with it to every living being first your body, And then all your possessions, followed by your virtuous acts. Imagine then that they have found the ultimate happiness, Free of all impurity. Now when you inhale your breath See it coming with the pain and cause of pain for every Living being, deep into the center of your heart; Imagine then that they are free of every pain there is. It's said that doing the practice in this way is especially powerful, For the reason that—because the mind and winds both move in tandem— You'll be able to avoid distraction, and keep tight recollection. record.english: When you do the practice of giving as you breathe out, think of the quantity of virtue you have in you from your acts of taking refuge, and observing the laws of karma and its consequences. Also imagine that you have some immaculate happiness to give, even though at this point we have yet to gain any. Do the act of giving all these, focusing on the those in the lower realms. See them reaching the higher realms as a result. Next take the quantity of virtue that you possess from following the path of the three trainings. Give it out to those in the higher realms, and imagine that Take finally the quantity of virtue you have from learning the Wish for enlightenment, and from following the way of life of the noble sons and daughters of the Buddhas. Imagine that you have given this virtue away to people like the listeners and the self-made buddhas. Imagine finally that this helps them reach Buddhahood itself.

record.english: The antidote for all these deeds is the nectar of the Dharma, spoken so true— and the further you turn from it then the more tightly you strangle your chances for the higher realms, and ultimate good. Death will rip away your life, and the wrongdeeds you have done will dragyou to the lower realms, to a fearful place of mighty and savage suffering, to the fires. And so I ask you, where could you find any thought more disastrous for you than this idea, that what is impermanent could ever be permanent?

record.english: The "power of destruction" refers to an emotion of regret. Imagine for example that four people have been sitting around a table eating the same dish mixed with some deadly poison. Now one of them has already fallen over and died. Another is taking his last breath. The third is writhing in agony. The fourth hasn't started feeling the effects yet. Think though of the unbearable regret that he has already begun to feel about eating that particular dish.

record.english: One might wonder about something else: Let's talk about the period while you are in the "uninterrupted" stage of the path of seeing [the actual direct perception of emptiness]. I can accept that at this point the negative thoughts eliminated by this path are no longer present, but we would have to say that the negative things eliminated by the path of habituation are still there, in a dormant way. At this particular point in time, the consciousness of the mind is unstained, unaffected by the mental seed which causes the mistaken state of mind where the appearance and actuality of things are different from one another. As such none of these things could lie dormant here, due to its very quality at the time. There is no consciousness of the senses that could act as the basis for those mental seeds, and it would be improper to say that physical form could ever provide such a basis either. According to you, moreover, there's no foundation consciousness. I would have to think then that there is no basis at all where these dormant things And yet there is no such problem, for at this point in time it is the simple "me" which is providing the basis for the dormant things eliminated by the path of habituation to stay. You can apply this reasoning as well to all the other cases involving things to be eliminated, and the antidotes which eliminate them. record.english: And suppose you agree to all that. But wouldn't it then be incorrect to say that someone had brought about their nirvana? And wouldn't it be incorrect to talk about the parts to a person having been destroyed, at a point in time when the person was still present? How could we have a knowledge of the end?

record.english: We would admittedly have to agree that Those Gone Thus have, in a nominal sense, attained enlightenment. But here is how it is that they cannot attain enlightenment in any ultimate sense. As described above, even Those Gone Thus are only persons who are projected upon the various parts to them. There is no One Gone Thus who exists in any other way: who is any one of the immaculate parts to them, individually; or who is the combination of these parts; or who is such that they are independent of these parts either.

record.english: And then from nowhere Came again a rainbow across the sky; The rainbow blazed In the marks and signs of an enlightened being-- There was a virgin, The cleft of method, the one of power, And then came a boy, Born of himself from the empty realm, Drunk from the wine Of the clear light of his home. They united, Never again to be apart: Friends and companions, Combined into a single thing. They tore from the others The immaculate, shining jewels And a mass of objects of enjoyment Claiming them then As their very own. When I think of this, I think of my Lama's kindness-- And oh how kind you have been to me, My Lama and my Lord.

record.acip: DE NAS BYAMS PA SGOM TSUL NI, RANG GI MA LTA BU YID DU GANG GCAGS PA CIG LA DMIGS NAS, 'DI LA ZAG MED KYI BDE BA GA LA YOD, ZAG BCAS KYI BDE BA TZAM YANG MI 'DUG ,
record.wylie: de nas byams pa sgom tshul ni, rang gi ma lta bu yid du gang gcags pa cig la dmigs nas, 'di la zag med kyi bde ba ga la yod, zag bcas kyi bde ba tsam yang mi 'dug
record.english: Next comes the meditation on love, which you do as follows.  First visualize a person sitting in front of you who is as appealing to you as your very own mother.  Then take yourself through this train of thought: How could this person in front of me have any pure happiness at all?  They don't even have any happiness of the impure kind.

record.acip: ,'GAG MED DU SNANG BA CHOS KYI DBYINGS, ,BDEN STONG DU 'CHAR BA SEMS KYI RGYUN, ,DBYER MED DU 'DRES PA'I RO GCIG PA, ,SEMS PA DE SEMS KYI RDO RJER SONG ,

record.english: The never-ending flow Of the empty realm of all things Showed itself to me: The stream of my own thoughts, The revelation That there is nothing that's real. And then that thought Melted into the diamond of the mind, A single song Of their indivisible union.

record.english: What these things look like is the various offerings.  What they have the power to do is to bring on an exceptional experience of pure bliss for the guests, by serving as the objects of their eyes and other senses. 14 Mantra for Inner Offering to the Slayer (Sadhana)

And we offer it to To our root and lineage Lamas: To You of greatest kindness, Crowning jewels of Enlightened Kind, Completely indivisible From the Keeper of the Diamond-- Lobsang Drakpa himself. Be pleased, we beg You, With our gift, and accept it from us. For we are high practitioners, And we ask that You grant us The power of the four mighty deeds, The eight great attainments, And the highest spiritual goal of all-- The unsurpassable.

record.english: Hung! Here is the Offering of the Gathering, Ecstasy itself, Blessed and become the nectar of deathlessness, Immaculate understanding. And we offer it To the glorious Diamond Lord of Terror, To the Slayer of the Lord of Death; And to all the millions of Close Angels, Peaceful ones and wrathful too: To those who count among Their number The Wheel of Time; the Secret Collection; Highest Bliss and the Diamond of Pleasure. Be pleased, we beg You, With our gift, and accept it from us. For we are high practitioners, And we ask that You grant us The power of the four mighty deeds, The eight great attainments, And the highest spiritual goal of all-- The unsurpassable.

record.english: Hung! Here is the Offering of the Gathering, Ecstasy itself, Blessed and become the nectar of deathlessness, Immaculate understanding. And we offer it To Those Who Have Gone to Bliss Before, or now, or in time to come; And to the highest Dharma, And the Community of beings Who have already seen the void; We offer it to all of You Jewels, Precious and supreme, Who cannot ever fail us. And most especially we offer this To the crowds of Warriors And Ladies who travel the sky. Be pleased, we beg You, With our gift, and accept it from us. For we are high practitioners, And we ask that You grant us The power of the four mighty deeds, The eight great attainments, And the highest spiritual goal of all-- The unsurpassable.

record.english: Hung! Here is the Offering of the Gathering, Ecstasy itself, Blessed and become the nectar of deathlessness, Immaculate understanding. And we offer it To the Six-Armed One, To the King of All Things, To the Empress of the Desire Realm, To the Four-Faced One, the Great King, The Arrogant One, and the Queen of Witches; To all the Guardians of the Dharma, To all the Ladies who keep it safe. Be pleased, we beg You, With our gift, and accept it from us. For we are high practitioners, And we ask that You grant us The power of the four mighty deeds, The eight great attainments, And the highest spiritual goal of all-- The unsurpassable.

record.wylie: hUM zag med ye shes bdud rtsir byin brlabs pa'i, ,bde ba chen po'i tshogs kyi mchod pa 'di, ,phyogs skyong zhing skyong dregs pa sde brgyad dang, ,tshe ring mched lnga bstan ma bcu gnyis sogs, ,yul lha gzhi bdag 'khor dang bcas la 'bul, ,dgyes shing bzhes nas sgrub mchog bdag cag la, ,spyod lam rnam bzhi bya ba ci byed kyang, ,kun slong ru nga phrag dog ma byed par, ,'gal rkyen kun gsol mthun rkyen ma lus sgrubs
record.english: Hung! Here is the Offering of the Gathering, Ecstasy itself, Blessed and become the nectar of deathlessness, Immaculate understanding. And we offer it To the Guardians of the Ten Directions, The Protectors of the Holy Lands, The Eight Great Forces of Arroganze, The Five Mighty Sisters who grant long life, The Band of the Twelve Protectors, And to all their like. We offier to the spirits of power Who live in our land, And to the lord of all the spirits Who make this very place their home. Be pleased, we beg You, With our gift, and accept it from us. For we are high practitioners, And regardless of how we seem to act, In each of the four different modes, You need not think of us With thoughts of envy or possessiveness. Come instead and work with us: Help to clear away Anything that could hinder us; Help us gather together All the things we need to succeed.

record.acip: RANG BDE MCHOG DANG RIG MA PHAG MOR BSKYED PA LUS LHA'I 'DU SHES DANG , GNYIS KA'I MKHA' GSANG BYIN GYIS BRLABS NAS YI GE BKOD PA SNGAGS KYI 'DU SHES DANG , THABS 'DI LA BRTEN NAS ZAG MED KYI BDE BA MNGON DU BYA'O SNYAM PA'I CHOS KYI 'DU SHES TE 'DU SHES GSUM DANG LDAN PAS SNYOMS 'JUG BYA,
record.wylie: rang bde mchog dang rig ma phag mor bskyed pa lus lha'i 'du shes dang , gnyis ka'i mkha' gsang byin gyis brlabs nas yi ge bkod pa sngags kyi 'du shes dang , thabs 'di la brten nas zag med kyi bde ba mngon du bya'o snyam pa'i chos kyi 'du shes te 'du shes gsum dang ldan pas snyoms 'jug bya
record.english: The practice of union must be performed with three different conceptions.  First, we must conceive of ourselves as the Angel named Highest Bliss, and our Woman of Knowledge as the Sow.  This is called "the conception of our body as the Angel." Secondly, we must bless the sky and the secret, placing the secret syllables.  This is called the "conception of the mantra."  Finally, we must have the "conception of the Dharma," which means that we think to ourselves, "By using this method, I will be able to bring about the bliss of the immaculate." *** Returning to Geshe Tsewang Samdrup:

record.acip: THIG LE DE RNAMS KYI NGO BO NI KHAMS DKAR DMAR 'DRES PA'I GONG BU YUNGS 'BRU TZAM PA RE YOD DO,,
record.wylie: thig le de rnams kyi ngo bo ni khams dkar dmar 'dres pa'i gong bu yungs 'bru tsam pa re yod do
record.english: The essential form of these drops is that each of them are little bits no larger than a mustard seed, in which the white and red elements are mixed together.

record.acip: RDO RJE'I RTZE MO NAS GTZUG TOR GYI 'KHOR LO RDZOGS PA'I BAR DU KHAMS DKAR PO'I THIG LE NYI KHRI CHIG STONG DRUG BRGYA GONG NAS GONG DU YAR BRTZEGS PA'I TSE, GTZUG TOR NAS RDO RJE'I RTZE MO'I BAR DU KHAMS DMAR PO'I THIG LE NYI KHRI CHIG STONG DRUG BRGYA 'OG NAS 'OG TU MAR 'BAB PAR GSUNGS SHING , DE LTAR KHAMS DKAR DMAR 'DZAG MED DU BCINGS PAS MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA NYI KHRI CHIG STONG DRUG BRGYA RDZOGS PA NA KHAMS DKAR DMAR GNYIS KYANG MED PAR 'GYUR TE,
record.wylie: rdo rje'i rtse mo nas gtsug tor gyi 'khor lo rdzogs pa'i bar du khams dkar po'i thig le nyi khri chig stong drug brgya gong nas gong du yar brtsegs pa'i tshe, gtsug tor nas rdo rje'i rtse mo'i bar du khams dmar po'i thig le nyi khri chig stong drug brgya 'og nas 'og tu mar 'bab par gsungs shing , de ltar khams dkar dmar 'dzag med du bcings pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba nyi khri chig stong drug brgya rdzogs pa na khams dkar dmar gnyis kyang med par 'gyur te
record.english: We pile up then 21,600 different drops of white element as we move higher and higher from the tip of the diamond all the way up to the chakra at the tip of the head.  It is stated that, when this is done, then 21,600 different drops of the red element drop further and further down, moving from the tip of the head to the tip of the diamond.  When we have gone this way through 21,600 different moments of immutable bliss with the white and red elements, locking them in so that they don't ooze out, then even these too--the white and red elements--also disappear.

record.acip: SNGAGS RIM LAS, BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS LUS LA 'DZAG MED DU BCINGS PAS MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA RDZOGS PA NA BEMS PO'I KHAMS THAMS CAD ZAD PAR 'GYUR BAS KHU BA NYID KYANG MI GNAS TE, ZHES PA NAS, DES NA STONG GZUGS KYI RDO RJE'I SKUR 'JA' TSON BZHIN DU SONG BA LA GROD PA 'O MAS BKANG BA BZHIN DU MA 'DZIN CIG ,CES GSUNGS PA'I PHYIR RO,,
record.wylie: sngags rim las, byang chub kyi sems lus la 'dzag med du bcings pas mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba rdzogs pa na bems po'i khams thams cad zad par 'gyur bas khu ba nyid kyang mi gnas te, zhes pa nas, des na stong gzugs kyi rdo rje'i skur 'ja' tshon bzhin du song ba la grod pa 'o mas bkang ba bzhin du ma 'dzin cig ,ces gsungs pa'i phyir ro
record.english: And this is true because of the section from the Steps on the Way of the Secret Word which begins with-- Suppose that we are able to lock the element of enlightenment into the body, so that it doesn't ooze out.  Our experience of immutable bliss then will be complete, and all the different parts of the material body will be put to an end.  When this happens, not even the semen itself then can remain. And continues up to-- We go then into the diamond body of empty form--something like a rainbow.  You shouldn't think though that the body just fills up the way an udder does with milk. [Translator's note: The 'DZAD MED of the original carving for 'DZAG MED here is an error; see the ACIP digital version, S5281, folio 394a.]

record.acip: DES NA SKU DE 'GRUB PA LA RDUL PHRA RAB TSOGS PA'I LUS NYAMS PAR BYA DGOS PAS, DE NI GSER 'GYUR GYI RTZIS LCAGS GSER DU BSGYUR BA BZHIN DU LUS LA BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS 'DZAG MED DU BCINGS PAS BEMS PO'I KHAMS RNAMS ZAD PAR BYED DE,
record.wylie: des na sku de 'grub pa la rdul phra rab tshogs pa'i lus nyams par bya dgos pas, de ni gser 'gyur gyi rtsis lcags gser du bsgyur ba bzhin du lus la byang chub kyi sems 'dzag med du bcings pas bems po'i khams rnams zad par byed de
record.english: It is though true that--in order to reach this holy body--the body which is composed of aggregates of atoms must be made to disappear.  As such, we must lock the element of enlightenment within the body, preventing it from oozing out.  This then can act like the alchemical elixir which turns iron into gold.  It brings all the various material parts of us to an end.

record.acip: ,KUN LA PHUL BAS ZAG MED BDE BAS TSIM, ,SEMS CAN RNAMS KYANG SGRIB BRAL CHOS SKU THOB, ,MCHOD PA'I 'KHOR GSUM SMRA BSAM BRJOD 'DAS KYI, ,BDE STONG GNYIS SU MED PA'I NGO BOR GYUR, CES DANG ,

record.english: We offer this then to You all; May You be filled With immaculate bliss. And may every living being Be freed from every obstacle, Achieving the body Of ultimate truth. May the three parts Of our offering Transform into indivisible Bliss and voidness, Beyond all words to tell.

record.english: Man and Woman, Lords of the Warriors, Glorious, Heruka, Master of emptiness, Stopping all projections, Reveling, forever, In the thousand pleasures Of the indestructible drop.
